variations.name: Gigascale green ammonia (electrolytic H2 + Haber-Bosch)
variations.description: Couples large renewable-powered water electrolysis to conventional Haber-Bosch synthesis to make fossil-free ammonia at million-tonne scale for fertilizer, shipping fuel, and hydrogen export, decarbonizing the single largest chemical CO2 source.
variations.white_space: Economics, not physics: green ammonia lands at roughly 2-3x grey cost, so projects live or die on subsidized offtake and dedicated shipping. A wave of 2025-26 FID failures (BP exiting AREH, Fortescue abandoning Queensland, Murchison's shipping deal collapsing) shows the bottleneck is bankable long-term buyers and logistics, not technology. Opening: aggregated demand/offtake vehicles (H2Global-style auctions) and merchant import terminals that de-risk the buyer side.

companies.name: NEOM Green Hydrogen Company (ACWA Power / Air Products / NEOM)
companies.what: Building the world's largest single-site green ammonia plant (1.2 Mtpa) on ~4 GW of solar+wind+storage with thyssenkrupp electrolyzers; Air Products is exclusive offtaker.
companies.signal: ~$8.4B financed; under construction, commissioning slipped from 2025 to 2027

companies.name: AM Green (Greenko)
companies.what: Retrofitting India's Nagarjuna/Kakinada fertilizer complex with electrolytic H2/ammonia backed by pumped-hydro-firmed renewables; 1 Mtpa phase one.
companies.signal: FID reached on first 1 Mtpa; Uniper offtake up to 500k tpy + Yara/Keppel; first shipments now targeted 2028

companies.name: ACME Group
companies.what: Developing green ammonia in India (Tamil Nadu) and Oman for export and domestic fertilizer auctions.
companies.signal: Won ~370k tpy of India's fertilizer-producer auction volume; secured ~INR 40B for Oman; Yara offtake 100k tpa from Oman phase 1 (start 2027)

companies.name: Fertiglobe / Scatec (Egypt Green Hydrogen)
companies.what: 100 MW electrolyzer feeding renewable H2 into Fertiglobe's existing Ain Sokhna ammonia plant — Africa's first integrated green H2 plant.
companies.signal: Phase one commissioned 2022; 20-year H2Global-backed offtake at EUR1000/ton; FID on full project targeted H1 2025

companies.name: Yara International
companies.what: World's largest ammonia trader/producer; operating green ammonia at Porsgrunn (Heroya) and signing binding offtakes (ACME, AM Green) to green its fertilizer book.
companies.signal: Heroya renewable ammonia unit operating; multiple long-term green NH3 offtake agreements

companies.name: CF Industries
companies.what: Largest North American ammonia producer; ran an electrolytic green ammonia project at Donaldsonville but pivoted capital to blue (CCS).
companies.signal: Dec 2025 management dropped the incremental electrolyzer investment for inadequate returns, favoring CCS

companies.name: Australian Renewable Energy Hub (BP / InterContinental Energy / CWP Global)
companies.what: Up to 26 GW Pilbara renewables for green hydrogen/ammonia export — emblem of the gigascale thesis.
companies.signal: BP exited as operator and equity holder July 2025 from the ~$55B hub; project's lead developer gone

companies.name: Murchison Green Hydrogen (CIP / Mineral Resources)
companies.what: ~$15B Western Australia green ammonia export project.
companies.signal: Effectively paused after NYK shipping deal collapsed (2026); FID now pushed to 2027

variations.name: Modular & distributed ammonia synthesis (relaxed Haber-Bosch)
variations.description: Shrinks Haber-Bosch into containerized, intermittency-tolerant units running at lower temperature/pressure via advanced catalysts or sorbent-enhanced loops, so farmers and ports can make green ammonia on-site instead of shipping it from gigafactories.

companies.name: Talus Renewables (TalusAg)
companies.what: Containerized 'talusOne' (~1.4 t/day) and 'talusTen' (~20 t/day) green ammonia systems sold with long-term farmer offtakes.
companies.signal: $22M Series A (Material Impact, Xora/Temasek); commercial units running in Kenya (Kenya Nut Co.) and Iowa (Landus); Angola project to 2028

companies.name: Tsubame BHB
companies.what: Low-temperature/low-pressure Haber-Bosch using Hosono's ruthenium-on-electride (C12A7:e-) catalyst for distributed plants.
companies.signal: Series C ~JPY5.3B; 2025 Global Cleantech 100; tech running at INPEX Kashiwazaki Hydrogen Park (~500 t/yr) and a Brazil (Atvos) LOI

companies.name: Starfire Energy
companies.what: 'Rapid Ramp' modular ammonia plants designed to follow variable renewable power, plus an integrated ammonia-cracking path.
companies.signal: $24M Series B; transitioned from grant- to investment-funded; scaling pilot plants

companies.name: Ammobia
companies.what: 'Haber-Bosch 2.0' loop pairing low-temperature catalyst with solid sorbents to cut synthesis-loop cost up to 50% (10x lower pressure, ~150C lower temp).
companies.signal: $7.5M seed (total $13.5M); backers include Shell Ventures, ALIAD (Air Liquide), MOL Switch; building pilot

variations.name: Electrochemical & lithium-mediated nitrogen reduction
variations.description: Skips Haber-Bosch entirely by reducing N2 to ammonia in an electrolyzer at ambient conditions — often via a lithium-mediated cycle (Li metal -> Li3N -> NH3) — promising direct coupling to renewable electricity but still fighting low efficiency and selectivity.
variations.white_space: Physics-limited: lithium-mediated and direct N2 reduction still post low Faradaic efficiency, modest rates, and energy use that trails optimized Haber-Bosch, so all credible players remain lab-to-bench. The opening is a continuous, high-current-density, stable electrolyzer (especially Li recovery/regeneration) — whoever cracks durability at industrially relevant rates first leapfrogs the field.

companies.name: Jupiter Ionics
companies.what: Australian modular reactor doing continuous lithium-mediated electrochemical N2 reduction from water, air and renewable power.
companies.signal: Raised ~US$9M (incl. A$2.5M seed led by Tenacious Ventures + ~$2M government); reactor scale-up, pre-commercial

companies.name: NitroVolt (formerly NitroFix / Nitrofix Solutions)
companies.what: Danish continuous-flow lithium-mediated electrolyzer aimed at on-farm distributed green ammonia/fertilizer.
companies.signal: EUR3.5M seed (EUR750K pre-seed before); investors incl. EIFO, EQT Foundation; moving lab tech to a farm demo unit

companies.name: Atmonia
companies.what: Icelandic one-step electrochemical ammonia synthesis from air/water using a proprietary precious-metal-free catalyst (co-developed catalyst search with Fujitsu HPC/AI).
companies.signal: ~$16.7M raised (ReykVC, Landvaettir); achieved lab-scale ammonia production Oct 2025; further funding scheduled 2026-27

variations.name: Plasma nitrogen fixation & on-farm nitrate
variations.description: Uses non-thermal plasma to split air's N2 and O2 into NOx that dissolves into water as plant-available nitrate (or enriches manure/slurry), enabling electricity-and-air fertilizer made at the farm with no Haber-Bosch and no CO2.
variations.white_space: Energy efficiency is the wall: plasma N-to-NOx still consumes far more energy per kg N than Haber-Bosch, which is why Nitricity pivoted from plasma nitrate to waste-derived organic fertilizer. Plasma survives where the value isn't bulk N but logistics/co-benefits (slurry enrichment, on-site liquid nitrate, ammonia-emission abatement); the opening is selling the avoided-transport and manure-management value, not commodity N.

companies.name: N2 Applied
companies.what: Norwegian on-farm plasma units that fix air N into nitrate and lock nitrogen into livestock slurry/digestate, cutting ammonia emissions while boosting fertilizer value.
companies.signal: ~15 years of development; commercial-pilot units across European farms

companies.name: VitalFluid
companies.what: Dutch plasma-activated-water (PLAN2FIX) units extracting N from air directly into irrigation water as nitrate.
companies.signal: EU Horizon (Plan2fix) supported; field pilots

companies.name: Nitricity
companies.what: US firm that built plasma-activated-water nitrate pilots, then pivoted to electrified organic fertilizer from almond-shell waste.
companies.signal: $50M raised; Delhi, California plant (~100x scale-up) breaking ground, sold out through 2028 — but now organic-fertilizer, not plasma nitrate

variations.name: Biological nitrogen fixation displacing synthetic N
variations.description: Engineers or formulates soil microbes (often gene-edited to keep fixing nitrogen even when synthetic fertilizer is present) that colonize roots and convert atmospheric N2 into ammonia in-field, shaving synthetic fertilizer use and N2O emissions.

companies.name: Pivot Bio
companies.what: Gene-edited nitrogen-fixing microbes (corn, small grains, and now cotton via CERT-N) applied to seed/soil to replace part of synthetic N at yield parity.
companies.signal: $430M Series D (DCVC, Temasek), ~$2B valuation, ~$618M total; 2025 field data shows ~37 lb/acre N reduction across 172 fields; targets $1B revenue by 2030

companies.name: Kula Bio
companies.what: Energizes a naturally occurring microbe (Xanthobacter) into a high-output nitrogen biofertilizer applied to the root zone.
companies.signal: ~$86.7M raised across 6 rounds (incl. $50M Series A); latest round Nov 2025

companies.name: Switch Bioworks
companies.what: Engineers microbes to win root colonization first, then switch on nitrogen production — tackling the persistence problem that limits biofertilizer performance.
companies.signal: ~$26.9M raised (incl. $17M seed led by Change Forces Capital) plus $2M ARPA-E grant (Jan 2025); pre-commercial field work

companies.name: Corteva Agriscience
companies.what: Markets biological nitrogen products (e.g., Utrisha N, and assets from its Symborg acquisition) through its global ag-input channel.
companies.signal: Large-cap incumbent embedding N-fixing biologicals into mainstream distribution

variations.name: Blue ammonia with CCS (retrofit and new-build)
variations.description: Keeps natural-gas-based ammonia but captures and sequesters the process CO2 (via autothermal reforming or capture on existing steam reformers), giving a lower-carbon, lower-cost-than-green bridge molecule that monetizes US 45Q credits.

companies.name: CF Industries
companies.what: Operating CO2 capture/sequestration at Donaldsonville and building an ATR low-carbon ammonia plant (Blue Point) with JERA and Mitsui.
companies.signal: Donaldsonville CCS began generating 45Q credits July 2025; Blue Point JV civil construction 2026, ammonia start-up ~2029

companies.name: Woodside Energy (ex-OCI Beaumont)
companies.what: Owns and is expanding the Beaumont, Texas low-carbon (blue) ammonia complex acquired from OCI.
companies.signal: Acquired OCI's clean ammonia project for ~$2.35B (2024); blue ammonia train commissioning phase

companies.name: ExxonMobil
companies.what: Provides CO2 transport-and-storage offtake underpinning third-party blue ammonia (incl. CF Industries) and its own Baytown low-carbon hydrogen/ammonia plans.
companies.signal: Landmark CO2 offtake/transport-storage agreements signed with ammonia producers

companies.name: Air Products
companies.what: Developing large blue hydrogen/ammonia at its Louisiana Clean Energy Complex with CCS.
companies.signal: Multi-billion-dollar Louisiana blue project; scope rationalized amid 2025 capex discipline

variations.name: N2O abatement & low-carbon nitric acid
variations.description: Installs tertiary/secondary catalysts in nitric acid plants that destroy nitrous oxide (a ~265x-CO2 greenhouse gas) and NOx, the cheapest large-scale lever to cut the fertilizer industry's non-CO2 climate footprint.

companies.name: Clariant
companies.what: EnviCat N2O-S tertiary catalyst removing >95% of N2O from nitric acid tail gas.
companies.signal: 50+ installs over ~20 years; GNFC India site cutting ~44,000 t/month CO2e since late 2024

companies.name: thyssenkrupp Uhde
companies.what: EnviNOx combined N2O/NOx abatement system (with BASF-made catalyst) for nitric acid plants.
companies.signal: CSBP (Australia) NAAN3 plant achieving >98% N2O removal, <1 ppmv outlet (2026)

companies.name: Topsoe
companies.what: NShield monolith catalyst for combined N2O/NOx abatement at abatement cost below typical CO2 prices.
companies.signal: Commercial product line deployed globally

companies.name: Yara International
companies.what: In-house N2O abatement catalyst technology deployed across its own and licensed nitric acid plants.
companies.signal: >90% N2O cut in fertilizer production; ~30 Mt CO2e/yr abated globally; CF's Verdigris project (2025) alone cuts >600k t/yr

variations.name: Green urea & alternative nitrogen products (green AN, CO2-to-urea)
variations.description: Takes green/low-carbon ammonia downstream into the actual products farmers and miners use — urea (made with captured or direct-air-captured CO2), low-carbon ammonium nitrate for fertilizer and explosives — closing the loop on finished-product, not just feedstock, decarbonization.
variations.white_space: Green urea carries a double penalty — it needs both green ammonia AND a clean CO2 source — so levelized costs (~$1000/t with DAC) sit far above grey until ~2030, leaving almost no pure-play. Green ammonium nitrate is further along because miners/explosives buyers (Orica) will pay a green premium and volumes are smaller. Opening: green AN for mining and civil works as the beachhead, with green urea waiting on cheap captured CO2 co-located with green ammonia.

companies.name: Fertiberia
companies.what: Produces the world's first low-carbon technical ammonium nitrate from green-hydrogen ammonia at Puertollano, Spain.
companies.signal: First industrial-scale low-carbon TAN blast (with Orica) June 2024; targeting EMEA mining/civil markets

companies.name: Orica
companies.what: Global explosives maker buying low-carbon AN to offer decarbonized blasting products to mining customers.
companies.signal: Completed first low-carbon AN blast in Spain (2024); building low-emission ammonia feedstock supply

companies.name: Yara International
companies.what: Markets Low-Carbon Footprint Ammonium Nitrate and develops green urea pathways off its renewable ammonia output.
companies.signal: Low-carbon AN product line launched; green NH3 feedstock from Heroya

companies.name: CSIRO (green urea synthesis program)
companies.what: Public-research effort developing carbon-neutral green urea routes coupling green ammonia with DAC/captured CO2 (Australia perspective).
companies.signal: Research/techno-economic stage; base-case green urea ~US$989/t with renewables at $71/MWh

variations.name: Ammonia cracking & ammonia-as-hydrogen-carrier
variations.description: Ships hydrogen as easy-to-liquefy ammonia, then 'cracks' it back into hydrogen at the destination (or burns/runs it directly), unlocking long-distance clean-energy trade and zero-carbon ship/data-center power using the existing ~20 Mt/yr ammonia shipping base.

companies.name: Amogy
companies.what: Integrated ammonia cracking + fuel cell powertrain for ships and distributed/data-center power; also licensing a low-ruthenium cracking catalyst.
companies.signal: >$270M raised (+$23M extension to ~$700M valuation, 2025); sailed ammonia-powered tugboat (2024); JGC pilot + 40 MW Pohang power deployment (2028-29)

companies.name: H2SITE
companies.what: Palladium-membrane reactors that crack ammonia and separate high-purity hydrogen in one unit, including the first onboard-ship cracker.
companies.signal: EUR36M Series B; EIC Accelerator funding for a flagship 1 TPD cracker at a NW-Europe port; commissioned first on-board cracker + PEM fuel cell system

companies.name: thyssenkrupp Uhde
companies.what: Licensed large-scale ammonia cracking technology for hydrogen import terminals.
companies.signal: Building 28 t/day demo cracker with Uniper (Scholven, online ~end 2026); framework for up to six plants totaling 7,200 t/day for Wilhelmshaven

companies.name: Uniper
companies.what: Energy major standing up ammonia import + cracking infrastructure to supply ~10-20% of Germany's 2030 hydrogen demand via Wilhelmshaven.
companies.signal: Demo cracker under construction; licensed thyssenkrupp tech for commercial terminal

variations.name: Low-carbon phosphate/potash processing & recovered-nutrient fertilizers
variations.description: Recovers phosphorus (and nitrogen) from wastewater, manure and process streams as struvite or calcium phosphate, and valorizes phosphogypsum waste, reducing reliance on mined, energy-intensive phosphate/potash and the eutrophication footprint of nutrient runoff.
variations.white_space: Recovered nutrients are real but tiny against mined phosphate/potash, and phosphogypsum valorization is mostly still research; struvite economics depend on wastewater-plant gate fees and local fertilizer offtake. Opening: regulatory tailwinds (EU nutrient-recovery mandates, P-runoff limits) plus rare-earth co-recovery from phosphogypsum could turn waste liabilities into byproduct revenue.

companies.name: Ostara Nutrient Recovery Technologies
companies.what: Recovers phosphorus from municipal/industrial wastewater as struvite, sold as Crystal Green slow-release fertilizer; also treats phosphogypsum pond water.
companies.signal: Deployed at wastewater plants worldwide since 2005; launched next-gen Crystal Green (CG P2X) and EU-organic-approved struvite (2025)

companies.name: Schwing Bioset
companies.what: Biosolids handling and nutrient-recovery (struvite/Bioset) systems for municipal and industrial sludge.
companies.signal: Acquired by Metawater (Apr 2025), folding into a larger water-tech platform

companies.name: NPHarvest
companies.what: Aalto-spinout membrane system that extracts pure ammonia and calcium phosphate from wastewater without heat or high pressure.
companies.signal: Commercializing energy-efficient nutrient recovery; integrates with existing WWTPs

companies.name: Seraplant
companies.what: Produces recycled phosphorus fertilizer from sewage-sludge ash via reactive-bonding, granulation and fractionation.
companies.signal: Operating recycled-P fertilizer production

companies.name: Mosaic / OCP (phosphate-potash majors)
companies.what: Mined-phosphate/potash incumbents pursuing lower-carbon processing and phosphogypsum reuse rather than nutrient recovery.
companies.signal: Global reuse of phosphogypsum ~35% (2024 IFA report); majors exploring valorization and rare-earth co-recovery
